api_analysis.hypothesis: The missing instance_norm_forward binding can be created by writing a kernels/instance_norm_binding.cpp that validates inputs, allocates output, calls the existing instance_norm_forward_launcher from custom_ops.cu, and registers the operator with the required pybind signature.
evidence: model_new.py calls cuda_extension.instance_norm_forward(x, weight, bias, eps).
custom_ops.cu exports extern \"C\" void instance_norm_forward_launcher with parameters out, x, weight, bias, eps, N, C, L, strides, and stream.
custom_ops_contract.json specifies the function signature instance_norm_forward(Tensor x, Tensor weight, Tensor bias, double eps = 1e-05).
No existing binding .cpp file exists for this operator, so compilation would fail at the pybind registration stage.
changes: Add kernels/instance_norm_binding.cpp containing the tensor wrapper function instance_norm_forward and REGISTER_BINDING registration.

The wrapper will check CUDA device, float32 dtype, weight/bias shape/dtype, compute N/C/L from x.size(), allocate output using torch::empty_like(x), and call the launcher with the current CUDA stream.
Use extern \"C\" declaration for the launcher with exact parameter types matching custom_ops.cu.
The pybind signature will be py::arg(\"x\"), py::arg(\"weight\"), py::arg(\"bias\"), py::arg(\"eps\") = 1e-05.
